description.summary: injecting input into a seat, and capturing it out

protocol.description:
This protocol gives a privileged client two things a remote-control or shared-input service needs and the core protocol deliberately withholds.
An injector feeds pointer, keyboard and touch events into a seat as if they came from a physical device. They go through the compositor's normal input path: they move the real cursor, change focus, trigger compositor shortcuts and reach whichever client has focus, exactly like local input.
A capture works the other way round, for sharing one keyboard and mouse between several machines. The client arms it on edges of the output layout; when the user pushes the pointer through an armed edge, the compositor hides the cursor, stops delivering pointer and keyboard input to its clients, and sends every event to the capture client instead, until the client releases it back at a position of its choosing.
Both are as powerful as a physical keyboard: an injector can type into any window, and a capture sees every keystroke, passwords included. Only privileged clients can bind the manager global. A compositor must not expose it to sandboxed clients.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_input_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory for crownos_input_injector_v1 and crownos_input_capture_v1 objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Objects created through it are unaffected.

request.name: create_injector

description.summary: create an input injector for a seat

request.description: Create an object through which input is injected into the given seat. Any number of injectors may exist at once; their events are merged into the seat in the order the compositor receives their frames.

request.name: create_capture

description.summary: create an input capture for a seat

request.description: Create an object through which the given seat's pointer and keyboard input can be captured. The capture starts out disarmed.

interface.name: crownos_input_injector_v1
interface.description:
Injects events into one seat. Events are grouped into frames: every request other than frame and destroy adds an event to the pending frame, and frame applies the pending events in order, as one logical hardware event, stamped with the frame's time. Nothing takes effect before frame.
Coordinates on an output are in the output's logical coordinate space, the space xdg_output reports: (0, 0) is its top-left corner and its logical size is its bottom-right. The compositor maps them through the output's position in the layout, so the client never needs to know the layout.
Keys and buttons that are still pressed when the injector is destroyed or revoked are released by the compositor, and touch points still down are cancelled, so a client that crashes mid-drag does not leave a button stuck.

entry.name: invalid_touch_id
entry.summary: touch_down reused an active id, or motion/up named an unknown id

entry.name: invalid_value
entry.summary: an enum argument is out of range

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the injector. A pending frame is discarded; pressed keys and buttons are released and touch points cancelled.

request.name: pointer_motion
request.description: Move the pointer by dx, dy logical pixels, as a mouse would. The pointer stays within the output layout.

request.name: pointer_motion_absolute

description.summary: move the pointer to a point on an output

request.description: Move the pointer to x, y on the given output, as a pen or a touchscreen in pointer mode would. A point outside the output is clamped onto it. An output that no longer exists makes this event a no-op.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x in the output's logical space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y in the output's logical space

request.name: button

description.summary: press or release a pointer button

request.description: Press or release a pointer button, identified by its evdev code (BTN_LEFT is 0x110; see linux/input-event-codes.h).

request.name: axis
request.description: Scroll along an axis. value is the continuous amount, in the same units as wl_pointer.axis. value120 is the discrete amount for wheel scrolling in 120ths of a detent, as wl_pointer.axis_value120; it is zero for continuous sources such as a touchpad.

arg.name: value120
arg.summary: discrete amount in 120ths of a detent

request.name: key
request.description: Press or release a key, identified by its evdev code (KEY_A is 30). The compositor translates it through the seat's keymap, so the client sends physical keys, not characters.

request.name: touch_down
request.description: Start a touch point at x, y on the given output. id identifies the point until touch_up or touch_cancel and must not belong to a point that is still down, or invalid_touch_id is raised.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x in the output's logical space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y in the output's logical space

request.name: touch_motion
request.description: Move touch point id to x, y on the output it went down on. An id that is not down raises invalid_touch_id.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x in the output's logical space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y in the output's logical space

request.name: touch_up
request.description: End touch point id. An id that is not down raises invalid_touch_id.

request.name: touch_cancel
request.description: Cancel every touch point of this injector, as when a touchscreen decides the contact was a palm.

request.name: frame
request.description: Apply every event added since the previous frame, in order, as one logical hardware event. time_usec is the event time in microseconds on CLOCK_MONOTONIC, split into two 32-bit halves; clients receive it, truncated to milliseconds, as the time of the resulting events. A frame with no events is allowed and does nothing.

event.name: revoked
event.description: The compositor or the user withdrew the injector's permission, or its seat went away. Later requests are ignored; the client should destroy the object. This is the last event sent on the object.

interface.name: crownos_input_capture_v1

description.summary: takes over a seat's input at the edge of the layout

interface.description:
A capture is in one of three states: disarmed, armed and captured.
While armed, the compositor watches the pointer. When a relative motion would move it past an armed edge of the output layout — an edge of an output that has no other output beyond it — the capture becomes captured and entered is sent. Absolute motion, from a tablet or an injector's pointer_motion_absolute, never triggers a capture, and neither does motion while a pointer button is held or a compositor grab (a window being dragged, a menu) owns the pointer.
While captured, the pointer does not move and no client receives pointer or keyboard events; the cursor is hidden; and every motion, button, axis and key event is sent to this object instead, grouped by frame events. The capture ends when the client sends release, or when the compositor ends it (for instance on a session lock), and either way released is sent and the capture returns to armed with the same edges.
At most one capture of a seat is captured at a time. When several are armed on the same edge, the one armed most recently wins.

entry.name: invalid_edges
entry.summary: arm was given bits outside the edge enum

entry.name: top
entry.summary: the top edge of the layout

entry.name: bottom
entry.summary: the bottom edge of the layout

entry.name: left
entry.summary: the left edge of the layout

entry.name: right
entry.summary: the right edge of the layout

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the capture. If it was captured, input returns to the local seat with the pointer where it entered.

request.name: arm

description.summary: choose the edges that start a capture

request.description: Replace the set of armed edges. Zero disarms the capture. Bits outside the edge enum raise invalid_edges. Changing the edges while captured takes effect after the capture is released.

request.name: release

description.summary: give input back to the local seat

request.description:
End the capture and put the pointer at x, y on the given output, in that output's logical coordinate space (clamped onto it). Typically the point on the edge the user is coming back through. An output that no longer exists puts the pointer back where the capture entered.
Sending release while not captured is not an error and has no effect: the compositor may have ended the capture itself just before.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x in the output's logical space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y in the output's logical space

event.name: entered

description.summary: the pointer went through an armed edge

event.description:
The capture is now captured. output is the output whose edge the pointer went through, edge is that edge (exactly one bit), and position is where along the edge it crossed, in the output's logical coordinate space: the x coordinate for the top and bottom edges, the y coordinate for the left and right ones.
Keys that were already pressed when the capture began stay pressed for the local clients and their releases are delivered locally; the capture receives only keys pressed after entered.

event.name: motion
event.description: Pointer motion in logical pixels, after the local acceleration profile, like the motion that would have moved the local cursor.

event.name: button
event.description: A pointer button, by evdev code, was pressed or released.

event.name: axis
event.description: Scrolling, in the same units as crownos_input_injector_v1.axis, so a remote end can inject it unchanged.

event.name: key
event.description: A key, by evdev code, was pressed or released. The code is the physical key, before any keymap.

event.name: modifiers
event.description: The seat's xkb modifier state, as wl_keyboard.modifiers reports it. Sent once right after entered, and again whenever it changes while captured.

event.name: frame

description.summary: end of a group of events

event.description: Ends a group of motion, button, axis, key and modifiers events that belong to one hardware event. time_usec is its time in microseconds on CLOCK_MONOTONIC, split into two 32-bit halves.

event.name: released

description.summary: input is back with the local seat

event.description: The capture ended, because the client sent release or because the compositor ended it, and the capture is armed again. No capture events follow until the next entered.
